title_original: ‘It reminds me of a bright star in the night sky’: Sophia Dom’s best phone picture
excerpt_original: After a storm, the artist relocated a detached flower head to a rainwater barrel, and was captivated by the harmonious composition Amateur photographer and artist Sophia Dom was gardening on a warm August afternoon when she took this photo. “My home town of Ivanovoa is sometimes…

blocks.text: A mateur photographer and artist Sophia Dom was gardening on a warm August afternoon when she took this photo. “My home town of Ivanovoa is sometimes referred to as Russia’s Manchester as it’s a major textiles hub,” she says. “I love spending time in my back yard, taking care of my plants and being in nature.”
She noticed that one flower had broken from its stem: “A cosmos,” she says. “It looked so tiny and defenceless that I felt sorry for it.”

There had been a huge storm in the previous few days, so her metal barrel for rainwater had filled to the brim. Dom gently relocated the lost flower to the barrel and as she did, a droplet fell from a tree branch into the pool below. When the ripples disturbed the surface, “the composition became not just interesting, but captivating”, she says. “By the time I grabbed my phone, the waves had faded, so I used my finger to mimic the effect.”

Dom, who also makes analogue collages using multicoloured velvet paper, “in avant-garde style”, says she finds inspiration and hope in art every day. “Here, I especially like the deep colours, balance and harmony in the composition, and the fragility of a flower in water. I hope it encourages viewers to take a pause from the hustle and bustle. It reminds me of a bright star in the night sky. The flower is, after all, named cosmos.”
